driver_ask.t: What should people know about {drv}, Chuck?
Who is {drv}, for anybody just joining us?
Chuck, put {drv} in context for me.
What is the story with {drv}, Chuck?

hist_reigning.t: He is the reigning champion, and that changes how a season feels. Everybody else is measuring themselves against him, and he knows it every time he looks in a mirror.
The number one on the car. It looks like an honour and it races like a target — every driver out here would rather beat him than beat anybody else.
He won it last year, which means he has already answered the only question that matters. Doing it again is a different problem, and a harder one.
Defending a championship is nothing like winning one. You spend the year protecting something instead of chasing it, and that gets into a driver's head.

hist_chasing.t: {titles} already, and he is here for {next_title}. At a certain point the trophies stop being the reason — it becomes about how far you can push the number.
He has {ntitles} of them. You would think that takes the edge off — in my experience it does the opposite. The more you win, the less you can stand not to.
{next_title} world championship. Very few drivers ever get near that, and the ones who do tend to be the ones who never learned how to be satisfied.
This is a man chasing {next_title} title. Nothing about that is normal, and nothing about the way he goes racing is normal either.

hist_champion.t: {titles}. Once you have proved you can do it over a whole season, you never quite stop believing you can do it again.
He has won a world championship. That is a whole year of not making the mistake, which is a completely different skill from being quick on a Saturday.
There is a title on his record, and you see it in races like this — he knows exactly which afternoons are worth risking something for.
A champion. People forget how much of that is patience: you cannot win one of those by being brave twenty times in a season.

hist_winner.t: {wins} in this sport, and no championship. That is the hardest career to have — good enough to beat anybody on his day, never quite in the right car for a year.
He has won {wins}. Every one of those is a Sunday where he was the best driver out there, and the record book will still call him a nearly man.
{nwins} victories. You do not do that by luck or by having the quickest car once — that is a driver who knows how to close a race out.
A Grand Prix winner, {wins} over. What he has never had is a whole season where the car was under him every weekend, and that is what a title needs.

hist_winless.t: He has never won one, and that is not a criticism. Most drivers who get this far never win a Grand Prix at all.
No victories yet. The first one is the hardest thing in this sport, because until you have it everybody quietly wonders whether you can.
Still waiting on that first win. He needs one afternoon where the car is good and the race falls his way, and then everything anybody says about him changes.
Nothing on the top step so far. I have known drivers who waited years for it and drove better afterwards than they ever did before.

hist_rookie.t: First full season. Everything he does out there he is doing for the first time, in front of everybody, against men who have been doing it for a decade.
He is learning this in public, which is the only way it has ever been done. The mistakes are part of it and so is being quick straight away.
A rookie year. The thing nobody tells you is how long the season feels when every circuit is new and every one of your rivals has been there twenty times.
New to all of this. Watch how he is on the opening lap — that is where you can see a rookie thinking, and where the good ones stop looking like one.

hist_new_team.t: First season at {team}. Changing teams looks simple from outside and it is not — new engineers, a new car underneath you, and a year to prove it was the right call.
He is in {team} colours now. Most drivers take half a season to stop driving the car they used to have, and you see it on corner entry.
New surroundings. The hardest part is not the car, it is learning which people to trust when something is wrong — and that takes a year, not a weekend.
{team} signed him and this is the season they find out. Both are being judged on a partnership that is a few months old.

hist_favourite.t: He is one of the names you would have picked before the season. Being favourite is its own weight: no credit for winning, all the blame for not.
Everybody expected him to be in the fight this year. That expectation does something to a driver, and the ones who handle it are the ones who win championships.
On paper this should be his season. On paper is where a lot of championships have been won and then not won.

hist_season_wins.t: He has {swins} this season, and you can see what it has done for him — a driver who has already won this year races differently to one who has not.
{swins} already this year. Confidence is not a thing you can put in a car, but it is the closest thing to free lap time there is.
He arrives here having won this season. That matters more than the points — he knows this car can do it, and so does everybody else.

hist_note.t: {drv}, {note}. That is the kind of thing that gets forgotten by the end of a season, and it is exactly what makes him worth watching now.
{drv}, {note}. It changes how you read everything else he does out there.
Remember this about him — {drv}, {note}. Careers turn on less.
{drv}, {note}. Whatever happens this season, that is the line people will use about him.
